comment: Every authored asset the yard's hulls may load. src/ships/ShipAssets.js loads ONLY what is declared here; scripts/tests/ship-assets.test.mjs holds every entry to the licence allow-list (generated, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0 with attribution, proprietary-owned) and re-runs the generator into a temp directory to prove the committed file is the one the script produces. A geometry entry's `parts` names the meshes inside the .glb and the MATERIAL KEY each one is drawn with - the loader reads the key off the mesh name and discards the glTF material unread, so an authored hull costs no shader program. `bytes` and `tris` are the on-disk size and the triangle total, both asserted by the test suite so a silently re-exported file cannot drift from its declaration. A file missing at runtime degrades to the procedural hull - see ShipAssets.js and the asset arm of Hulls.buildKestrel.
